entities.name: Angkor Wat & Angkorian Inscriptions
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary:
The corpus of over 1,200 stone inscriptions from the Angkor period of the Khmer Empire (c. 802–1431 CE), written in Sanskrit and Old Khmer, found at Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom, Preah Khan, Banteay Srei, and other temple sites across Cambodia. These inscriptions — particularly the foundation steles placed at temple dedications — record royal genealogies, territorial claims, religious endowments (specifying hundreds of temple servants, dancers, and annual provisions of rice), irrigation works, and legal decrees.

The inscriptions at Angkor Wat itself, commissioned by King Suryavarman II (r. 1113–c. 1150 CE), establish the temple's dedication to Vishnu and the king's claim to divine authority. French scholars of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (George Coedès, Claude Jacques) deciphered and published these inscriptions, enabling the reconstruction of Khmer history.
